transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Yeah, hi. Um... I guess I came in because for a really long time now, I’ve just been walking around with this... this flat, heavy feeling. Like, even when work is going okay or people are being nice to me, I still feel down and just kind of empty most days. 

Actually, work has been pretty okay lately. We just got this new analytics software at the firm last week. It's supposed to make pulling the management reports way faster, but honestly, the user interface is a complete nightmare. My manager, Dave, he spent like 45 minutes on a Teams call yesterday just showing off the new pie chart features. I don't even know why we'd use pie charts for our risk assessments, you know? It doesn't make any sense for the kind of metrics we track, a bar graph is obviously better for year-over-year comparisons. But anyway, yeah, even when Dave is in a good mood about the software or things are fine at the office, I just... I still have that heavy, empty feeling.
Have you noticed any changes in how you feel about activities or hobbies you used to enjoy? Like, do you still take pleasure in them, or do they feel more like a chore now?

Um, hobbies... I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed a huge change, or maybe I just don't have a lot of hobbies to begin with? I used to play some video games, mostly strategy stuff, but honestly, my laptop is getting so old it can barely run anything anymore. The fan sounds like a jet engine taking off. I was looking at buying a new one, maybe something with a dedicated graphics card, but the prices right now are just insane. Like, who has two grand to drop on a gaming rig when rent is what it is? My buddy Mark just bought one, and he's always trying to get me to play online with him, but he plays those first-person shooters, and I just... I don't have the reflexes for that. Plus, he always wants to play at like 11 PM on a Tuesday. Like, dude, some of us have to be on a Teams call with Dave in the morning, you know? But yeah, I don't know, I guess I just haven't really thought about if I enjoy things less. I just kind of exist.
Would you say that you feel depressed or down most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, I mean, like I was saying when I first got here, it's pretty much all the time. Every day. I just have this flat, heavy thing I'm carrying around. Even when people are being perfectly nice to me, I just feel down and empty for most of the day. 

Like, the guy at the deli downstairs from my office is always super nice. He remembers my order and everything—turkey on rye, no tomato. But honestly, lately they've been putting way too much mayo on it. I don't get why places do that, you know? It completely ruins the structural integrity of the bread. By the time I take the elevator back up to my desk, the bottom half of the sandwich is just total mush. Dave actually went down there and complained to the manager about his own sandwich once, which was incredibly awkward to stand there and watch. He made this huge deal about the mustard-to-meat ratio, like it was a corporate crisis or something. He literally drew a diagram on a napkin. But anyway, yeah... even when I'm just sitting there eating my lunch, or when things are totally fine, I still just feel really down.
How long have you been feeling this way most days?

Um, how long... I guess I've been thinking about that. It's been going on for about two years and two months now. It started right around the time this big dashboard project happened and kind of put me in the spotlight at work. 

Which, honestly, was a complete nightmare to build. They wanted us to pull all this legacy data from the old system, but the old system was literally just a giant shared folder of Excel sheets that this guy Gary had been hoarding. And Gary had just retired and moved to like, Boca or something, so nobody knew how any of his macros worked. I spent weeks just trying to figure out his color-coding system. He used three different shades of blue to mean completely different things. Like, why would you use sky blue for 'pending' and navy blue for 'escalated'? They look exactly the same on those cheap standard-issue monitors they give us. I actually had to put in a ticket with IT just to get a monitor where I could tell the difference, and the IT guy, Kevin, gave me so much grief about it. He acted like I was asking for a solid gold keyboard, and then it still took him three weeks to bring it up to my desk. 

But... yeah, anyway, ever since that dashboard project happened and everyone was looking at my work, I've just felt this way pretty much every day.
Have you noticed that you don't take as much pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy, or do you find that nothing really feels enjoyable anymore?

Um, enjoyment... I don't know, I guess I haven't really noticed a change in that? Like I was saying earlier about hobbies and stuff, I just kind of exist. But I wouldn't say I've lost interest or that nothing is enjoyable, I just... I don't know, I haven't really thought about it. 

I guess I've been too busy dealing with the new guy they hired to replace Gary. His name is Todd, and he is just... he's something else. He came in on his first day wearing a full three-piece suit. To a back-office analytics job. Everyone else is in khakis and polos, and Todd looks like he's about to close a million-dollar real estate deal. And he insists on bringing in these incredibly smelly lunches. Like, yesterday he microwaved leftover fish curry in the breakroom at 11:30 in the morning. The entire floor smelled like a fish market for the rest of the day. Dave was practically gagging during our afternoon stand-up. I actually had to go down to the deli just to get away from the smell, which is when I got that soggy sandwich I was talking about. It's like a chain reaction of bad lunch decisions. 

But, uh, yeah, sorry, what were you asking? Oh, right, enjoyment. Yeah, I don't really have an answer for that. I haven't really noticed losing interest in things, I just feel down all the time.
Have you noticed that you feel fatigued or have a lack of energy most days, even when you haven’t been doing much physically or mentally taxing?

Yeah, my energy is... well, it's pretty much non-existent. By the afternoon, I’m so wiped out that even doing the smallest things, like fixing a basic spreadsheet error or finishing my expense paperwork, it just feels like I’m dragging my body and my brain through mud. 

Which, to be fair, the expense paperwork is a total nightmare right now anyway. They just migrated us to this new portal system last month, and it is completely broken. You have to upload digital receipts, but the system only accepts files under two megabytes. Like, my phone's camera automatically takes photos way bigger than that. So I literally have to email the picture of my deli receipt to myself, open it on my desktop, resize it down so it looks like a blurry postage stamp, and then upload it. And if you accidentally select 'client meeting' instead of 'business meal' from this tiny drop-down menu, this woman in accounting, Brenda, rejects the entire month's report. She won't even tell you which line item is wrong, she just hits reject and sends this passive-aggressive automated email. Dave tried to push back on it last week and she CC'd his director. It's like a weird power trip for her. 

But... yeah, sorry. Just thinking about it makes me tired. But it's not just work stuff that does it, it's everything. Even just getting myself to soccer after work feels like that same dragging-through-mud feeling. I just don't have the energy for any of it.
Have you found yourself feeling worthless or guilty about things, even when there’s no real reason to feel that way?

Um, worthless... I don't know if I'd use that word, but I definitely feel... I don't know, like a fraud, maybe? Like, people at work still bring up that dashboard I built, and they act like it's this great thing, but my first thought is always that I somehow fooled them. And then every time I miss a follow-up or send an email late, it just feels like proof that I’m not actually as capable as they think I am.

Which, speaking of emails, the new email client they pushed to our laptops over the weekend is an absolute disaster. They switched us from Outlook to this weird proprietary web-based thing, and it doesn't even have a functioning search bar. Like, how do you release an email client in this day and age without a search function? I had to find an email from Dave from three weeks ago about the Q3 projections, and I literally had to scroll manually through hundreds of messages. And the font! They changed the default font to something that looks like Comic Sans's ugly cousin. I tried to change it back in the settings, but it's locked by the administrator. So now every time I email the VP of Operations, it looks like I'm sending a party invitation instead of a data analysis. Kevin in IT said it's a "known issue" and they're "working on a patch," but we all know that means it's never getting fixed. 

But, um, yeah, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling guilty or whatever. Yeah, I just feel like I'm tricking everyone and they're going to figure it out eventually.
Have you noticed that your thinking has slowed down or that it's harder to concentrate on tasks, even simple ones?

Concentration? Um, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed any issues with my thinking slowing down or anything like that. I mean, I can still focus on things when I need to, it's just that I'm so tired all the time. 

But honestly, the real problem with concentrating at work right now is the new open-plan office layout. They decided to knock down all the cubicle walls over the weekend to "foster collaboration," which is corporate speak for cramming more desks into the same space. So now I'm sitting directly across from Todd—the three-piece suit guy—and I can hear every single time he clears his throat, which is about every four minutes. And he types so loudly! It's like he's angry at the keyboard. He practically punches the keys. 

Plus, they put these weird brightly colored bean bag chairs in the middle of the floor for "impromptu brainstorming sessions." Nobody uses them except for this guy from marketing who comes over, sits in the neon green one, and takes his shoes off. Like, actually takes his shoes off in the office. I tried to bring it up to HR, but they just sent me this generic link about embracing modern workplace culture. 

So, yeah, it's pretty hard to concentrate when you've got a guy in a suit hammering on his keyboard on one side and a guy in socks on a bean bag chair on the other. But, um, my actual thinking? No, I haven't noticed my brain slowing down or anything like that. I don't really have that problem.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently, like losing or gaining a significant amount without trying?

Weight? Um, no, I don't think so. My clothes all still fit exactly the same, so I haven't really gained or lost anything that I've noticed. 

Which is actually kind of surprising considering they completely ruined the lunch situation at the office this month. They decided to gut the breakroom and get rid of the normal vending machines, and they replaced them with these "smart" fridges that are supposed to promote corporate wellness. But it's literally just fourteen-dollar salads in plastic bowls and these weird cold-pressed juices that taste like actual lawn clippings. And you can't even just swipe your card to get something. You have to scan a QR code, download a third-party app, make an account, and link your credit card just to unlock the fridge door. 

I spent twenty minutes on Tuesday just trying to buy a sparkling water. The app crashed three times, and then it charged my card twice without even unlocking the door. I asked Kevin in IT about it, and he said the third-party vendor handles all the refunds, but when you call their customer service number, it just goes straight to a full voicemail box. So now nobody uses the fridges, and everyone is just ordering delivery every day. Which means the lobby is constantly packed with delivery drivers, and the security guard, Stan, is absolutely losing his mind trying to figure out who ordered from where. He started making people come down and show him the order confirmation on their phones before he'll let them take the bags. 

So, yeah, it's a whole ordeal just to eat lunch now. But, um, anyway... what was the question? Oh, weight. Yeah, no changes there. I'm pretty much exactly the same.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have slowed down, or that you feel restless or agitated without a clear reason?

Um, slowed down? No, I don't think my speech or movements are slow. And I'm not really restless or anything either. I mean, I sit at a desk all day, so I'm pretty stationary. 

Although, speaking of sitting at my desk, they just replaced all our office chairs on Wednesday. They brought in these ergonomic stool things that are supposed to engage your core or whatever. It's basically half a bouncy ball attached to a stick. You can't even lean back. Todd—the guy I mentioned earlier—tried to lean back to stretch yesterday, and the whole stool completely rolled out from under him. He spilled his coffee all over his desk, and it dripped down onto the power strip, which shorted out the entire pod's monitors. 

So then we all had to sit there for an hour waiting for facilities to come mop it up and reset the breaker, while Todd stood there trying to dab his pants with these tiny brown paper towels from the bathroom that don't actually absorb anything, they just sort of move the liquid around. And of course, the guy in the bean bag chair didn't even notice because he had his noise-canceling headphones on. 

It's just... it's a circus. I don't even know why they bother changing these things. But, um, what were you asking? Oh, right, moving slow or being restless. Yeah, no, I haven't really had any of that. I just sit on my bouncy stool and try not to fall over.
Have you ever felt like life isn't worth living or had thoughts about ending your life?

Ending my life? Um, no. No, I've never thought about anything like that. I mean, I'm just tired all the time, but I don't want to die or anything. 

Though, I will say, if I have to sit through one more of Greg's mandatory "synergy" meetings, I might actually lose my mind. He's our department head, and he went to this leadership seminar in Aspen last month, and now he makes us start every Monday morning with a ten-minute guided meditation. In the middle of the open office. We're supposed to close our eyes and focus on our breathing, but all I can focus on is Todd breathing heavily through his nose right across the desk from me. 

And last week, during the "silent reflection" part, the marketing guy on the bean bag chair actually fell asleep and started snoring. Like, really loudly. Greg didn't want to interrupt the "flow of energy," so we all just had to sit there for five minutes listening to this guy snore while Greg kept softly whispering about visualizing a mountain. It's just so ridiculous. I spend half my week dealing with this stuff instead of actually analyzing any management data. 

But, um... what were we talking about? Oh, right. No, I don't want to hurt myself or anything. I definitely don't have those kinds of thoughts.
Have you found that you have trouble making decisions, even small ones, or that you can't think clearly like you used to?

Trouble making decisions? Um, no, not really. I mean, my brain works fine, I don't have any issues thinking clearly or picking things. 

Which is good, because trying to get anything done at my office requires, like, a ridiculous amount of mental gymnastics right now. They just implemented this new "hot-desking" policy on Monday. So instead of having our own desks, we have to log into this portal every morning at exactly 8:00 AM to reserve a workspace for the day. But the system is completely bugged. If you click the map too fast, it assigns you to a desk in the basement storage room. And you can't cancel it once it's booked. 

So yesterday, I ended up having to work at a tiny folding table right next to the industrial shredder. Every time someone came down to shred documents, the table vibrated so hard my mouse would click on things by itself. And Todd, of course, forgot to log in entirely, so he didn't get a desk at all. He tried to just sit in the breakroom, but remember those smart fridges I was talking about? They were doing maintenance on them, so there were just three guys in overalls yelling over each other while Todd tried to have a client Zoom meeting on his laptop. He had to keep muting himself because one of the repair guys kept swearing at the QR code scanner.

It's honestly just exhausting dealing with the logistics of simply existing in that building. But, um... sorry, I lost track again. What was the question? Oh, right, decision making and thinking clearly. Yeah, no, I'm fine with that. I don't have any trouble there.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have slowed down, or that you feel restless or agitated without a clear reason?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? About moving slow or being restless? Yeah, like I said, no, I don't really have any of that. I'm pretty normal when it comes to moving and talking. 

Although, if you want to talk about moving slow, you should see the elevators in my office building right now. They're doing renovations on the executive floor, so they shut down three of the four elevator banks for the contractors. Now everyone in a fifteen-story building has to use one single elevator. Yesterday, I waited in the lobby for twenty minutes, and when I finally got in, this guy from accounting—Dave—squeezed in with his folding electric scooter. He refuses to lock it up in the garage. So we're all packed in like sardines, and his scooter tire is just pressing right into my leg, getting street dirt all over my pants. 

And then the elevator stopped on the sixth floor and just sat there. The doors wouldn't open, and it started making this horrible grinding noise for like five minutes. Dave actually suggested we establish a "survival hierarchy" in case the cables snapped. He's so weird. 

But, um... sorry. Yeah, to answer your question again, no, I haven't noticed my speech or movements slowing down or feeling agitated or anything. Just the elevators.
Have you found that you no longer care about things you used to care about, or that activities you used to look forward to now feel meaningless or uninteresting?

Care about things? Um, no, not really. I mean, I still care about the same stuff I always have. I haven't lost interest in my hobbies or anything like that. 

Though, speaking of hobbies, I used to really like playing in this rec league softball team with some guys from the office, but the league got taken over by this new commissioner, Steve. Steve takes it way too seriously. Like, we're a bunch of analysts and HR reps playing on a Tuesday night, and he shows up with a literal radar gun to clock our pitches. Last week, he instituted a mandatory uniform policy, which means we all had to buy these itchy, polyester jerseys that say "Pitch Please" on the front. I mean, really? 

And the worst part is, he keeps trying to implement "advanced analytics" into our lineup. He made this massive Excel spreadsheet tracking everyone's on-base percentage and slugging metrics. He actually benched Todd—yeah, the same Todd from my desk pod—because his "launch angle" wasn't optimal. Todd just wanted to drink a beer and stand in right field, and now he's sitting in the dugout keeping score on an iPad while Steve yells about defensive shifts. It completely ruined the vibe. I honestly just stand in the outfield now hoping the ball doesn't come to me so Steve won't analyze my throwing mechanics.

But, um... sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, losing interest in things. Yeah, no, I still like doing stuff. Just not Steve's version of softball.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have slowed down, or that you feel restless or agitated without a clear reason?

Wait, did you just ask me that again? About moving slow or being restless? I feel like we just talked about that. But yeah, like I said before, I haven't noticed anything like that. My speech and movements are totally normal. 

Though, if you want to talk about restless, you should see my cat, Barnaby, right now. I don't know what his deal is lately, but he has been absolutely out of his mind. I bought him this new automated laser pointer toy because I thought it would keep him occupied while I'm dealing with the whole hot-desking nightmare at work. But instead of just chasing the laser, he's figured out how to knock the actual machine off the coffee table so it points at the ceiling. 

So now, at like 3:00 AM, he's just launching himself off the back of the sofa, trying to catch a red dot on the ceiling fan. And the worst part is, he keeps missing and landing on my pile of clean laundry. I had to go to work yesterday with white cat hair all over my dark blue slacks. Todd actually asked if I was wearing a mohair suit. I mean, who even wears mohair anymore? 

But, um... anyway, what were we saying? Oh, right, moving slow or feeling agitated. Yeah, no, I'm fine. Just Barnaby is the restless one.
Have you noticed that you don't take as much pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy, or do you find that nothing really feels enjoyable anymore?

Wait, are we doing a loop? I swear you just asked me about not caring about things or losing interest in stuff. I mean, my answer is still the same. No, I still enjoy things just fine. Nothing's really changed there.

Well, except maybe my interest in going to the grocery store. Have you seen the prices lately? It's ridiculous. I went to get my usual brand of coffee the other day—just the store brand, nothing fancy—and they completely redesigned the packaging. It used to be this nice, simple brown bag, and now it's this shiny, holographic foil thing that looks like it belongs on a spaceship. And of course, they shrank the bag by like four ounces but raised the price by two dollars. 

I asked the cashier about it—this kid who looked like he was maybe sixteen and definitely did not want to be there—and he just shrugged and said it was "shrinkflation." Then he tried to get me to sign up for their new rewards program, which requires you to download an app that tracks your location at all times. I mean, why does the grocery store need to know where I am when I'm not buying coffee? Are they going to send me a push notification when I walk past a Starbucks? It's so invasive. I ended up just leaving the coffee on the belt and walking out. Now I'm drinking this instant stuff I found in the back of the pantry that expired in 2021. It tastes like dirt, but at least it didn't come in a holographic bag.

But, uh... sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, enjoying things. Yeah, no, I still enjoy things. Just not grocery shopping anymore.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have slowed down, or that you feel restless or agitated without a clear reason?

Wait, seriously? Are you reading off a script or something? Because I'm almost positive you literally just asked me about moving slow or being restless like two minutes ago. I feel like I'm taking crazy pills here. But no, for the third time, my speech and movements are fine. I'm not restless, I'm not agitated. 

I mean, the only thing that's making me agitated right now is this whole hot-desking situation at work. I don't know if I mentioned it, but it's an absolute nightmare. They brought in this consulting firm—probably a bunch of 22-year-olds like me who think they know everything about "corporate synergy"—and they decided we didn't need assigned desks anymore. They call it "agile working." 

So now, every morning, it's like the Hunger Games just to get a chair with lumbar support. If you don't get there by 7:45, you're stuck at this high-top table near the kitchen that smells like burnt popcorn and microwave fish. And you have to carry all your stuff in this little plastic locker caddy. I feel like I'm in middle school carrying a shower caddy to the communal bathroom. Yesterday, I sat down at a desk, and the guy before me had left a half-eaten tuna sandwich in the drawer. Who puts a sandwich in a drawer? 

Anyway, it's just really frustrating because I used to have my own desk, with my own monitor height, and my little succulent plant that Barnaby hasn't eaten yet. Now I'm just a nomad in a sea of gray carpet. 

But, um... sorry, what were you asking? Oh, right, being restless. Yeah, no, I'm not restless. Just annoyed about the desks.
